ork Requirements

jobs.title: Project Manager, AMI
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Project Manager, AMI based in United States.

This role offers the opportunity to lead complex Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) and utility technology initiatives from planning through implementation. You’ll manage projects for electric, gas, and water utilities, coordinating diverse teams, vendors, and technical workstreams. Your work will span areas such as feasibility, business cases, procurement, deployment, systems integration, testing, and operational readiness. You’ll serve as a trusted project leader, balancing scope, schedule, budget, resources, risks, and client expectations. The role combines strategic oversight with hands-on project execution and regular interaction with executives and technical stakeholders. It’s an ideal opportunity for an experienced utility project manager who enjoys solving complex challenges and driving meaningful transformation across the energy and utilities sector.

Accountabilities

Lead AMI projects: Manage day-to-day delivery of complex AMI and related utility technology initiatives from project initiation through implementation and transition to operations.
Own project planning: Develop and maintain integrated project plans covering schedules, budgets, milestones, dependencies, resources, deliverables, and critical activities.
Coordinate cross-functional teams: Align utility business, IT and OT teams, technical specialists, AMI vendors, system integrators, field contractors, and other third parties.
Manage risks and issues: Identify emerging challenges, track risks, issues, decisions, actions, assumptions, and changes, and drive timely resolution or escalation.
Facilitate communication: Lead project meetings, executive briefings, workshops, and cross-functional working sessions, ensuring stakeholders remain aligned on priorities and decisions.
Oversee vendors: Monitor vendor performance and contractual commitments, including milestones, deliverables, dependencies, acceptance activities, and implementation progress.
Coordinate AMI workstreams: Support alignment across meter and network deployment, systems integration, testing, data readiness, operational readiness, change management, and customer-facing activities.
Deliver executive reporting: Provide concise, decision-oriented updates covering project status, schedule, budget, risks, issues, dependencies, and upcoming decisions.
Maintain project governance: Ensure effective documentation, project controls, and governance practices while developing trusted client relationships and identifying opportunities to create additional value.
Manage resources and financials: Forecast project resource requirements, maintain resource bookings, monitor financial performance, and support accurate monthly invoicing and revenue forecasting.

Requirements

Professional experience: 5+ years of project or program management experience within the utility industry, with demonstrated experience supporting or managing AMI implementations for electric, gas, or water utilities.
AMI expertise: Working knowledge of key AMI components, including meters and endpoints, communications networks, head-end systems, meter data management systems, systems integration, testing, deployment, data management, and operational readiness.
Project management: Proven ability to manage complex schedules, budgets, risks, issues, dependencies, changes, resources, deliverables, and executive reporting.
Technology implementation: Experience coordinating complex, cross-functional technology programs involving utility business teams, IT and/or OT organizations, vendors, system integrators, and field resources.
Communication and facilitation: Strong interpersonal and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate effectively with executives, technical specialists, business stakeholders, vendors, and field personnel.
Problem solving: Ability to identify project challenges, develop practical courses of action, facilitate decisions, and drive issues through resolution.
Adaptability: Comfortable working independently in environments where information may be incomplete, priorities can evolve, and projects involve multiple stakeholders.
Collaboration: Effective in hybrid, virtual, and in-person environments with geographically distributed teams.
Technical proficiency: Proficiency with project management tools and Microsoft Office applications; experience with Microsoft Project or comparable scheduling software is a plus.
Education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.
Certifications: PMP or a comparable project management certification is preferred.
Work authorization: Candidates must be authorized to work for any employer in the United States or Canada. Employment visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

Benefits

Compensation: $140,000–$170,000 USD per year, plus an annual bonus; actual compensation may vary based on experience.
Remote work: Remote position when not traveling to client sites.
Travel: Up to 50% travel, depending on project and client requirements.
Healthcare: Medical, dental, and vision insurance options.
Insurance coverage: Company-paid life insurance and short- and long-term disability insurance.
Flexible spending: Medical and dependent-care flexible spending account options.
Parental support: Paid parental leave.
Time off: Flexible Time Off (FTO) policy, subject to manager approval and business coverage requirements.
Retirement: 401(k) plan with a 3% employer match.
Professional growth: Opportunities to develop project management and utility industry expertise while contributing to meaningful technology initiatives.
Collaborative culture: A thoughtful, curious, knowledge-driven environment that values clarity, substance, collaboration, and continuous growth.
Meaningful impact: Work on initiatives that help utilities navigate complex technology programs and shape the future of energy and utility services.

jobs.description:
About Engine

Engine is the all-in-one travel and spend management platform trusted by 38K+ businesses and groups representing 1.8M+ travelers. We're the retailer and the rails of business travel, the fastest-growing company in travel tech, built on a decade of proprietary technology, supply, and pricing no one else can replicate. Other travel and AI companies run on our infrastructure to book real trips, hold rates, and move payments, without building any of it themselves. We built it, AI-forward at every layer, from how travelers book to how the rails run.

That work has earned recognition as one of Fast Company's Best Workplaces for Innovators (2025), TravelTech's Reservation Platform of the Year (2026), and one of Built In's Best Places to Work (2020–2026).

We're looking for bold, ambitious people to help redefine how businesses manage and experience travel. Working here, you can expect exponential growth, an ambitious pace, full ownership, and high-caliber colleagues who push you to do the best work of your career. Every hire raises the bar.

Come outpace the ordinary and build the future of travel with us.

About the Role

At Engine, we're transforming business travel — and doing it with unparalleled speed, heart, and hustle. Our most important work is always in motion, and it needs operators who can keep the engine running fast — and fix what's breaking before anyone else notices it's broken.

As a Senior Program Manager, you own team outcomes across a complex initiative. You're highly skilled at what you do, and you bring that specialization to bear on situations that don't come with a manual. You diagnose unusual problems through sophisticated analysis, adapt proven methods when playbooks run out, and communicate with the kind of clarity that earns credibility with peers and senior stakeholders alike.

You'll sit within our centralized Business Operations function — a pool of PGMs deployed where the work is hardest. You drive your work independently, syncing to check quality and alignment rather than waiting for direction. When something is complex or genuinely novel, you engage the right people — not because you need to be told what to do, but because you weigh context carefully and know when a second perspective adds value.

What You'll Do

Own initiative outcomes end-to-end — and begin taking on responsibility outside your immediate lane when the work demands it.
Diagnose complex, ambiguous situations using deep knowledge in your area — assessing root cause and resolving a wide range of issues through creative problem-solving.
Adapt protocol when needed — you apply proven methods in novel situations, not just when the playbook applies.
Drive work independently, syncing regularly to check quality and alignment — you manage your own pace and escalate with context, not confusion.
Critically weigh context, data, and tradeoffs to make smart decisions that support team goals — you interpret thoughtfully before you act.
Communicate with clarity and precision — you adapt your messaging across teams to reduce misalignment and move work forward, and you help teammates navigate uncertainty or conflict with confidence.
Earn credibility with peers and senior collaborators through consistent, high-quality delivery — your reputation is built on follow-through.
Identify AI and automation opportunities within your domain — you test, iterate, and build toward repeatable approaches with confidence, distinguishing genuine leverage from marginal improvement.

What We're Looking For

Deep program management experience with meaningful XFN ownership — you've driven complex initiatives across multiple teams and stakeholder groups, and your track record shows it.
Sophisticated analytical and problem-solving ability — you assess ambiguous situations through deep specialization and resolve issues creatively when standard approaches don't fit.
Independent operator with sound judgment — you drive your work without being asked, sync proactively, and engage others when the situation is genuinely complex or novel.
Clear, direct communicator — you adapt messaging across audiences, write and speak with precision, and provide thoughtful input that helps others navigate difficult situations.
Strong cross-functional instincts — you earn credibility with peers and senior collaborators through delivery, not just relationship-building.
AI-curious and action-oriented — you identify where automation creates real leverage in your domain and build toward repeatable approaches.
High-growth tech or SaaS experience preferred.

Applications for this role will be accepted through 11/11/26 or until the role is filled. We encourage you to apply early, as we may begin reviewing applications before the deadline.

Compensation

Our compensation packages are based on several factors, including your experience, expertise, and location. In addition to a competitive base salary, total compensation may include equity and/or variable pay (OTE). Your recruiter will share your complete compensation package as you move through the process.

Base Pay Range

$99,700—$138,000 USD

The Engine Edge: Perks & Compensation

We believe in rewarding great work with great benefits:

Compensation:
Competitive base pay tied to role and experience, with opportunities for bonuses, commissions, and equity.
Benefits:
Check out our full list at engine.com/culture.
Environments for Success:
Different roles have different needs in terms of the environments that drive success which is why we have a hybrid-hub model. Whether you are in one of our amazing offices or fully remote, we'll make sure you have what you need to succeed.

Perks and benefits may vary based on employment type, location, and more.

and play a pivotal role in shaping the future of partner education, enablement and experience across Australia and the broader APAC region.

Be at the Centre of Strategic Change

This is not a traditional project management role.
You'll work across some of Pax8's most exciting and business-critical initiatives, helping bring structure, momentum and measurable outcomes to projects that directly influence partner success. From supporting new market expansion and partner transformation programmes to enhancing educational experiences and operational excellence, you'll help turn ambitious ideas into reality.

As Pax8 continues its journey as a technology-first, AI-enabled organisation, you'll have the opportunity to work at the intersection of innovation, learning, partner engagement and business transformation. You'll help shape programmes that scale globally while building skills and experience that keep pace with rapidly evolving technology.

🌟 Why Pax8?

Pax8 is transforming the way small businesses access and adopt technology. Through our cloud marketplace, partner ecosystem and growing AI capabilities, we're helping Managed Service Providers deliver better outcomes faster.
We're ambitious, collaborative, people-first and deeply focused on continuous improvement. You'll join a business where ideas are welcomed, ownership is encouraged and the impact of your work is visible across the organisation.

📋 What You'll Be Responsible For

You'll be trusted to lead programmes from concept through delivery, ensuring teams stay aligned, risks are proactively managed and outcomes are achieved.
Key areas of focus include:
Leading strategic projects across the Partner Experience function
Building and maintaining programme roadmaps aligned to business priorities
Establishing governance frameworks, reporting structures and stakeholder communications
Coordinating cross-functional teams to deliver outcomes on time and within scope
Facilitating planning workshops, steering committees and programme reviews
Tracking milestones, dependencies, budgets, risks and delivery performance
Supporting large-scale learning, enablement and educational initiatives
Driving operational improvements that increase efficiency and programme scalability
Partnering with Marketing, Sales, Content and Partner Experience teams on growth initiatives
Supporting change management activities that encourage adoption and engagement
Creating clear executive reporting, insights and recommendations
Maintaining accurate project documentation, decisions, actions and outcomes

🎯 The Impact You'll Make

Success in this role means more than delivering projects.
You'll help partners access better learning experiences, support strategic growth initiatives across APAC, improve internal ways of working and ensure critical programmes generate measurable business value. Your ability to bring clarity, structure and execution discipline will enable teams across Pax8 to move faster and deliver more for our partners.

✅ What We're Looking For

We're interested in talented project professionals who thrive in complex, fast-moving environments.

You'll likely bring:

Extensive experience leading projects and programmes from initiation to completion
Strong project governance, planning and delivery expertise
Proven ability to develop business cases, project frameworks and success measures
Exceptional stakeholder management and influencing skills
Experience working across multiple teams and competing priorities
Demonstrated success managing risks, dependencies and complex deliverables
Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities
Confidence presenting to senior stakeholders and leadership teams
Experience delivering projects within technology, SaaS, distribution, enablement or partner-focused environments
Familiarity with Agile, Waterfall or hybrid delivery methodologies
Experience using project and collaboration platforms such as Monday.com, Jira, Asana, Smartsheet, Microsoft Project or similar tools
The ability to navigate ambiguity, identify gaps and create practical solutions

You'll stand out if you're comfortable building structure from complexity, enjoy solving challenging business problems and aren't afraid to raise issues early to keep programmes on track.

🛡️ Trust and Hiring

At Pax8, we care deeply about building genuine, trust based relationships — starting with how we hire.
To protect our business, our teams, and our customers, we use a range of measures throughout the recruitment process to help confirm authenticity and prevent fraud. These safeguards are designed to be fair, respectful, and proportionate, and may evolve as risks change. By applying, you acknowledge that we take steps to verify identity and representation during hiring. If you're applying as your authentic self, you have nothing to worry about — we're excited to meet you.
We also use thoughtfully applied AI-enabled tools to support our hiring process. These tools may assist with tasks such as reviewing or prioritising applications, but hiring decisions are made by our people. More information is available in our Recruitment Privacy Notice. If you have questions about how we hire or would prefer not to have your application supported by these tools, you can opt out at any part of our process.

🌍 Inclusion Matters

We encourage you to apply even if you don't meet 100% of the criteria. We're committed to diverse perspectives, inclusive hiring and sharing your transferrable skills. To fulfil this role, you must hold valid right to work in Australia.

💰 Reward, Recognition & Benefits
:
Competitive salary
Employee Share Ownership opportunities
Annual bonus programme
Dedicated learning and development investment
LinkedIn Learning access
Health and wellbeing support
Flexible hybrid working
Paid volunteering opportunities
Employee Assistance Programme
Regular social and team events
Access to industry-leading technology training and certifications

🏢 Hybrid Working

This opportunity can be based in Sydney, Melbourne or Brisbane
.
Our offices provide collaborative, modern environments designed to support creativity, connection and innovation. You'll benefit from flexibility while maintaining meaningful in-person collaboration with colleagues across the business.

📈 Accelerate Your Growth

There's extensive room for a talented individual to grow at pace — whether that's advancing quickly in this role or exploring one of the many opportunities across our global organisation. You'll have access to our internal development hub designed to accelerate your skills and stretch your potential. Alongside specialist Learning & Development trainers, you'll also tap into AI powered tools, "born in the cloud" mentors, and cross continent collaboration that broaden your perspective and sharpen your expertise. We'll give you the space, trust, and the right projects to help you thrive — and full visibility of what it takes to reach your next level.

❤️ About Pax8

Our mission is to build the managed intelligence marketplace and empower small businesses to do more with smarter technology. We are a fast-growing, dynamic, and high-energy organisation with a start-up feel, allowing you to make a meaningful impact on the business. Culture is also important to us, and at Pax8, it's business, and it IS personal. We are passionate, creative, and unconventional. We work hard, keep it fun, and expect the best! We Elev8 each other. We Advoc8 for our partners. We Innov8 continuously. We Celebr8 life.

🔍 Background Checks

As part of our hiring process, we are required to undertake pre-employment checks on all candidates that are successful in their application with Pax8. As part of these checks Pax8 will request ID verification, reference requests and qualification checks (additional checks may be completed for certain countries, such as criminal and financial). All checks are completed by our third-party provider, First Advantage. Once checks have been completed all candidates will receive a copy for their records.

jobs.title: Lead Project Manager (Swedish speaker)
jobs.description:
Celonis is the trusted platform to industrialize Enterprise AI. At our core is the Celonis Context Model — which combines process data, business knowledge, and intelligence into a living digital twin of the enterprise that AI can actually understand, turning AI's operational blind spots into operational clarity. World's leading companies trust Celonis and its global ecosystem of partners to make their AI agents, people, systems, and processes work together, achieving transformational outcomes. We believe there's a massive opportunity to unlock global productivity and sustainability by giving AI the context to understand how every business process really works. Join our mission to make processes work for people, companies, and the planet.

The Team

Celonis Services is the delivery engine of our Celonis Customer Organization, responsible for turning the Celonis platform into measurable, business-critical outcomes for our customers. In the AI era, our role has elevated: as AI agents like our own Apollo take on more of the technical build, our people focus on the work that drives real impact—understanding our customers' business-critical problems, designing the solutions that solve them, and quantifying the value delivered. Our Deployment Engineers and Deployment Architects pair deep domain and industry expertise with serious platform mastery and AI-augmented delivery, directing agentic systems while owning the judgment, architecture, and customer relationships that AI cannot replace. We deliver faster and smarter than ever, and we own the outcome: solution go-live, solution adoption, initial value realization support and the long-term success of our customers.

The Role:

As a Lead Project Manager
, you will support end-to-end implementations of Celonis’ technology across our largest and most strategic customers. You will articulate Celonis’ product positioning to customers and collaborate with Sales, Partners and Value Engineering to establish Celonis’ Services Value proposition and create statements of work with customers during the pre-sales phase.

In this role, you will assist customers in understanding how to build best practice and enduring capabilities, are responsible for identifying further Services needs by the customer whilst engaged and responsible for customer satisfaction throughout a customer's engagement with Celonis.

Fluency in Swedish language is required.

The work you’ll do:

Lead complex transformational customer programs, shape and define the project outcome and then steer towards it.
Planning, scheduling, and management of project timelines and activities from project kick-off through to training, ensuring each project is delivered on time and meets the customers' requirements.
Manage resources, schedule, scope and budget on multiple projects by creating and maintaining detailed project plans that emphasize speed to delivery and maximise the efficient use of resources needed to meet the requirements.
Collaboration with senior executives, process owners and technical teams within each customer to understand their goals, objectives and requirements and to ensure their successful implementation. You will be their primary point of contact for product feature requests and escalation of support issues.
Regularly communicate project status, covering key discussion items, action items, risks and issues. Keep projects up to date in the Celonis Professional Services Automation System to enable accurate and timely project and portfolio reporting.
Proactively manage and escalate risks and issues internally to Celonis management and externally to customer project sponsors to minimize impact to project success.
Provide guidance and mentoring to the implementation team, including partner resources, to ensure Celonis methodology is being followed.
Use your experience to contribute to the continual improvement of Celonis Services methods as well as the maturing field expertise and best practices.

The qualifications you need:

Client-facing Project Management experience in enterprise software implementations, managing multiple projects concurrently.
Extensive experience in project management disciplines, including documenting and maintaining project plans, risk/issue/action logs, and driving problem resolution in partnership with customers and Celonis executives.
Strong communication skills and a background in consulting with a proven ability to manage stakeholders and project timelines.
Experience in people managing consulting teams both onshore and offshore.
Experience in positioning Services, writing proposals and “statement of works” within a complete ecosystem (customers and partners).
A history of working with an ecosystem of partners and managed co-delivery.
Ability to effectively set and manage customer expectations.
Strong analytical skills, especially in applying technology solutions to core business problems.
Ability and willingness to be certified in Celonis products.
Project management certifications (PMP, Prince2, or Safe/Agile).
Bachelors or Masters in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics or other related field.

What Celonis can offer you:

Pioneer Innovation: Work with the global leader in Process Mining and the Process Intelligence Graph to shape the future of AI-driven business operations.
Ownership from Day 1: Every full-time Celonaut is an owner, receiving Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) and merit-based refresh grants.
Unrivaled Family Support: Benefit from our inclusive parental leave policy—24 weeks of fully paid leave for primary carers and 12 weeks for supporting carers, available from your first day of employment.
Work-Life Integration: Enjoy Unlimited PTO (in applicable regions) and generous PTO globally, as well as a flexible hybrid work model that balances remote focus with vibrant office collaboration.
Continuous Growth: Elevate your skills through our 70-20-10 learning framework, mentorship programs, and access to a dedicated learning platform.
Holistic Well-being: Prioritize your health with subsidized Wellhub memberships, mental health counseling, and dedicated Wellness Weeks that prioritize work/life balance.
Drive Sustainability: Participate in annual Impact Days, where you receive paid time off to volunteer for community and environmental causes with your local office, or virtually.
Global Inclusion & Belonging: Find community through our Inclusion Think Tank and participate in our annual Inclusion Days, ensuring every voice is heard and valued.
Value-Driven Impact: Join a mission-led organization where our core values—Live for Customer Value, The Best Team Wins, We Own It, and Earth Is Our Future—drive every decision.

About Us:

Celonis is the trusted platform to industrialize Enterprise AI, empowering organizations to analyze, design, and operate AI-driven processes. The Celonis Platform is powered by the Celonis Context Model, which combines process data, business knowledge, and intelligence to create a living digital twin of the enterprise that AI can understand — turning AI’s operational blind spots into operational clarity. Industry-leading companies around the world trust Celonis and its global ecosystem of partners to make their AI agents, people, systems, and processes work together, achieving transformational outcomes. Celonis is headquartered in Munich, Germany, and New York City, USA, with more than 20 offices worldwide.

Get familiar with the Celonis Process Intelligence Platform by watching this video.

Celonis Inclusion Statement:

At Celonis, we believe our people make us who we are and that “The Best Team Wins”. We know that the best teams are made up of people who bring different perspectives to the table. And when everyone feels included, able to speak up and knows their voice is heard - that's when creativity and innovation happen.

Any information you submit to Celonis as part of your application will be processed in accordance with Celonis’ Accessibility and Candidate Notices

By submitting this application, you confirm that you agree to the storing and processing of your personal data by Celonis as described in our Privacy Notice for the Application and Hiring Process.

This role is responsible for the oversight, management, and continuous improvement of the 3rd Party Quality Agent program, by establishing programmatic standards, driving accountability, and enabling effective coordination between Meta's on-site teams, 3rd Party Agents, General Contractors (GCs), Engineers of Record (EORs), OEMs, and internal Design Engineering stakeholders. Through effective leadership and partnerships, the DD&D Quality Program Manager will leverage program core competencies to drive quality outcomes ensuring predictable on-time delivery of our global campuses.

Quality Program Manager, Data Center Design and Construction Responsibilities:

3rd Party Agent Program Management
Maintain and update the Standard Scope of Work (SOW) Template for 3rd Party Quality Agents
Assign and allocate 3rd Party Agents to sites based on project needs and resource availability
Execute and manage 3rd Party Agent contracts
Lead the vetting and onboarding process for new 3rd Party Agents as program needs arise
Lead business reviews for 3rd Party Agents to evaluate performance, capacity, and alignment with program goals
Assess Agent performance and escalate performance issues to Agent Account Representatives
Conduct monthly 3rd Party Agent syncs for overview of site summaries, identifying trends, and receiving/providing feedback to and from suppliers, GCs, trade partners, manufacturers, etc
Program Oversight & Stakeholder Onboarding

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, R&D
jobs.description:
About SandboxAQ

SandboxAQ is a high-growth company delivering AI solutions that address some of the world's greatest challenges. The company’s Large Quantitative Models (LQMs) power advances in life sciences, financial services, navigation, cybersecurity, and other sectors.

We are a global team that is tech-focused and includes experts in AI, chemistry, cybersecurity, physics, mathematics, medicine, engineering, and other specialties. The company emerged from Alphabet Inc. as an independent, growth capital-backed company in 2022, funded by leading investors and supported by a braintrust of industry leaders.

At SandboxAQ, we’ve cultivated an environment that encourages creativity, collaboration, and impact. By investing deeply in our people, we’re building a thriving, global workforce poised to tackle the world's epic challenges. Join us to advance your career in pursuit of an inspiring mission, in a community of like-minded people who value entrepreneurialism, ownership, and transformative impact.

The Opportunity

R&D teams solve problems nobody has solved before. That's exactly what makes them hard to ship: the scope shifts as the science reveals itself, and the roadmap you set in January may need to look different by June, due to new results changing what “done” means.

We're looking for a Technical Program Manager who has run point on programs like this before.We’re especially interested in cases where the stakes were high enough that a missed milestone was expensive, publicly visible, or both. You've been the person who saw a bottleneck three weeks before it became a crisis. You've translated between scientists who need room to explore and finance/product stakeholders who need a defensible number. And, you know how to build a roadmap that's rigorous enough to hold people accountable and flexible enough to survive contact with real research.

You'll partner directly with our R&D department head and Product and Engineering to set ROI-optimal strategy, then own the execution machinery that turns that strategy into shipped, on-time, drama-free, and defensible results.

Key Responsibilities

Anticipate bottlenecks before they're bottlenecks. Work with R&D and Product to define requirements, surface technical dependencies, and build delivery schedules that account for trade-offs before they become fire drills.
Translate between three different languages. R&D needs room to be wrong in productive ways. Product and Engineering need specificity and commitments. Finance needs predictability against ROI. You'll build the shared vocabulary and cadence that lets all three coexist without anyone feeling boxed in or left in the dark.
Design execution rituals that fit a scientific team:sprints, checkpoints, and reviews that create accountability without forcing lab-paced work into a factory-paced cadence.
Own the roadmap end-to-end: build it, defend it, update it as the science evolves, and make sure it stays a living tool rather than a document nobody trusts.
Drive resourcing conversations with leadership and finance, making the case for what R&D needs and when, backed by a track record they can trust.
Get launches out the door cleanly. When a milestone, paper, or product moment is on the line, you're the person orchestrating the last mile. You’ll coordinate the handoffs, catch the loose thread, and make sure it lands without a scramble.
Play a critical role in reshaping drug discovery, advancing machine learning, and protecting humanity from disease.

Essential Skills & Experience

8+ years in technical program management or a similar role, with real experience sitting inside, rather than just tracking the status of, R&D or deep-science teams that shipped world-class products.
A track record, proven by specific moments you can point to, of stepping into a program mid-crisis (a stalled milestone, a resourcing gap, a scope blowup) and getting it back on track.
Demonstrated ability to build and defend ROI-generating roadmaps for teams doing genuinely novel, high-uncertainty scientific work.
Proven ability to get fluent in a new scientific domain fast enough to make good calls in it independently as demonstrated by either or both of:
An advanced degree in a technical field, or
Deep experience working within heavily scientific teams.

Experience partnering directly with finance and product leadership to tie technical delivery to investment decisions.
A bias toward asking "how might this plan break in six months?" before it does. You plan for your own team's disruption, not just external risk.

Highly Desired Skills & Experience

Experience at a startup, or in another environment where the roadmap changed faster than the org chart could keep up.
Direct biotech or biopharma experience.
Degree in machine learning and/or a drug-discovery-related field.
Experience standing up program management tooling, dashboards, or automation pipelines that a scientific team actually kept using.

Why Join Us?

We offer a comprehensive and competitive benefits package designed to support your health, financial well-being, and life outside of work.

Compensation: Competitive base salary, performance-based incentives or bonuses (where applicable), and equity participation.
Benefits: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage for employees and dependents with generous employer premium contributions, retirement savings with company matching, paid parental leave, and inclusive family-building benefits.
Work-Life Balance: Flexible paid time off, company-wide seasonal breaks, and support for flexible work arrangements that enable sustainable performance.
Career Development: Opportunities for continuous learning and growth through on-the-job development, cross-functional collaboration, and access to internal learning and development programs.

SandboxAQ Welcomes All

We are committed to fostering a culture of belonging and respect, where diverse perspectives are actively sought and valued. Our multidisciplinary environment provides ample opportunity for continuous growth - working alongside humble, empowered, and ambitious colleagues ready to tackle epic challenges.

Equal Employment Opportunity
: All qualified applicants will receive consideration regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or Veteran status.

Accommodations
: We provide reasonable accommodations for individuals with disabilities in job application procedures for open roles. If you need such an accommodation, please let a member of our Recruiting team know.

jobs.description:
Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at grafana.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

The Opportunity

Grafana's Demand Generation team is responsible for creating and accelerating pipeline across the full customer journey — from first touch through expansion. We run a modern, AI-forward operation: lifecycle email programs driven by an AI engine, territory-level buying signals surfaced directly to sales leaders, and agentic workflows that handle work that used to take teams of specialists.

. Minimum qualifications:

Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
8 years of experience in management consulting, product management and strategy, or analytics in a technology company.
Experience working with education institutions to drive programmatic engagement and collaboration across multiple projects while analyzing data and leading program reporting.
Experience designing, building, and managing a monitoring function, including developing metrics and dashboards to track progress and generate evidence-based insights and quantifiable impact.

Understanding of strategic planning frameworks (e.g., OKRs) and experience managing operational cadences with external partners.

Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills to identify trends and generate actionable insights.
Exceptional executive communication skills to synthesize complex project statuses, research findings, and impact data for executive leadership.

About The Job

Product and Business Strategy Leaders bring together teams across Google’s functions to help products execute optimally. Our team pushes Google to scale at key points that refine our products and infrastructure by executing efficiently, bringing solid business sense and sound judgment, and working effectively across organizational lines.

Our roles often include components of strategy (e.g. analyzing and understanding new trends in the industry, building business plans), operations (e.g. running the cadence of organizations, connecting the operating lines between our functions), and communications. Our team partners with senior leadership to run important functions that cross-cut our existing organizations and deliver high impact projects. We help Engineers, PMs, UX, and all of our other functions to build amazing products that delight our users, and then get those products into their hands.

In this role, you will drive our institutional collaboration sandboxes, fostering ongoing engagement with a consortium of schools, researchers, and organizations. You will manage partnerships between Google’s product/research teams and external institutions to solicit user feedback and test AI products in real-world contexts, collaborating heavily with cross-functional partners.

You will serve as the primary liaison for external higher education organizations and university stakeholders, while coordinating across internal Product, Research, Legal, and Partnerships teams. You will require an independent perspective and the ability to run smooth, efficient processes that create qualitative insight and quantifiable impact across multiple workstreams.

Your goal is to ensure these programs run seamlessly, generating evidence-based insights into how AI can improve educational outcomes and guiding how we build products to support that mission.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $150000 - $218000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits

Responsibilities

Learn more about benefits at Google .

Lead the full lifecycle execution of institutional collaboration sandboxes, serving as the primary driver for the program.
Act as the central point of contact, ensuring seamless and cohesive collaboration between external education organizations, researchers, and internal Google Product, Research, and Engineering teams.
Design, build, and own the monitoring and data function for collaborative engagements. Develop metrics, dashboards (e.g., using SQL, Looker), and processes to solicit user feedback, generate evidence-based insights, and quantify the impact of AI products in real-world contexts.
Synthesize complex project statuses, research findings, and quantifiable impact data into structured, persuasive written and verbal communications for executvie Google leadership and external dialogue.

and play a pivotal role in shaping the future of partner education, enablement and experience across Australia and the broader APAC region.

Be at the Centre of Strategic Change

This is not a traditional project management role.
You'll work across some of Pax8's most exciting and business-critical initiatives, helping bring structure, momentum and measurable outcomes to projects that directly influence partner success. From supporting new market expansion and partner transformation programmes to enhancing educational experiences and operational excellence, you'll help turn ambitious ideas into reality.

As Pax8 continues its journey as a technology-first, AI-enabled organisation, you'll have the opportunity to work at the intersection of innovation, learning, partner engagement and business transformation. Pax8 is transforming the way small businesses access and adopt technology. Through our cloud marketplace, partner ecosystem and growing AI capabilities, we're helping Managed Service Providers deliver better outcomes faster.

Leading strategic projects across the Partner Experience function

Establishing governance frameworks, reporting structures and stakeholder communications

Facilitating planning workshops, steering committees and programme reviews

Driving operational improvements that increase efficiency and programme scalability
Partnering with Marketing, Sales, Content and Partner Experience teams on growth initiatives
Supporting change management activities that encourage adoption and engagement
Creating clear executive reporting, insights and recommendations
Maintaining accurate project documentation, decisions, actions and outcomes

You'll help partners access better learning experiences, support strategic growth initiatives across APAC, improve internal ways of working and ensure critical programmes generate measurable business value. The ability to navigate ambiguity, identify gaps and create practical solutions

jobs.title: M&A Program Manager
jobs.description:
Nota Consulting is seeking an experienced M&A Program Manager to lead complex mergers, acquisitions, integrations, carve-outs, and value creation initiatives for our clients. This role is responsible for managing enterprise-wide programs from transaction close through execution, partnering with executive leadership to deliver integrations, separations, TSA management, synergy realization, and operational transformation. The ideal candidate has a strong consulting background, exceptional program management skills, and experience leading cross-functional M&A programs across Finance, HR, Technology, Operations, Legal, Supply Chain, and Commercial functions. This individual will thrive in fast-paced environments, providing structure, governance, and executive-level communication to ensure successful outcomes.

M&A Program Manager Location: Alexandria, VA — In Office 4 Days per Week
Overview Nota Consulting is seeking an experienced M&A Program Manager to lead complex, high-impact transaction and value creation programs for our clients. Our work includes M&A integrations, corporate carve-outs and divestitures, TSA management and exits, and post-transaction value creation initiatives.
These are high-stakes, fast-moving programs with significant financial and operational impact. Our Program Managers work directly with senior executives and cross-functional leadership teams to bring structure to complex situations, solve problems quickly, drive accountability, and ensure critical transaction milestones are achieved. Success requires a high level of ownership, attention to detail, sound judgment, and a willingness to put in the effort required during critical periods of a transaction.
This position is based in the Washington, DC area and requires in-office attendance four days per week. We believe our best work is delivered through close collaboration, rapid problem-solving, mentorship, and strong team connection. Working together in person is an important part of how we develop our consultants, collaborate across engagements, and maintain the culture and standards of our firm.

ResponsibilitiesM&A Program Leadership Lead complex M&A integrations, carve-outs, divestitures, TSA programs, and value creation initiatives from planning through execution.
Establish and manage Integration Management Offices (IMO), Separation Management Offices (SMO), Program Management Offices (PMO), and associated governance structures.
Develop and maintain integrated program plans across multiple functional workstreams, including critical milestones, dependencies, risks, issues, decisions, and critical path activities.
Drive Day 1 readiness, Day 100 execution, TSA exits, integration and separation milestones, and longer-term transaction objectives.
Take ownership of program outcomes and proactively identify and resolve issues that could jeopardize transaction timelines or business continuity.

Integration & Carve-Out Execution Coordinate complex cross-functional workstreams spanning Finance, HR, Legal, Technology, Cybersecurity, Supply Chain, Operations, Commercial, Procurement, and Shared Services.
Manage TSA planning, governance, execution, and exit activities, ensuring dependencies and deadlines are actively managed.
Lead separation planning for carve-outs and divestitures, maintaining focus on Day 1 business continuity and the establishment of standalone capabilities.
Drive integration planning and execution following acquisitions, ensuring functional plans remain aligned with the transaction thesis and overall integration strategy.
Identify and proactively manage cross-functional dependencies, risks, resource constraints, and decisions requiring executive intervention.

Value Creation Support post-transaction value creation programs, including synergy realization, cost savings, operational improvement, organizational redesign, and process optimization.
Translate strategic objectives and investment theses into executable initiatives, milestones, owners, and measurable outcomes.
Partner with executive leadership to identify opportunities to accelerate value capture and improve operating performance.
Establish and monitor KPIs, synergy targets, cost savings, and other benefits-realization measures.

Executive Governance & Stakeholder Management Serve as a trusted advisor to senior executives and functional leaders throughout the transaction lifecycle.
Lead executive steering committees, governance forums, workstream meetings, and program reviews.
Develop concise, decision-oriented executive presentations, dashboards, status reports, RAID logs, and decision materials.
Drive accountability across workstream leaders and teams, ensuring commitments are met and issues are addressed quickly.
Communicate complex issues clearly and confidently, including when programs are under pressure or require difficult decisions.

Consulting & Firm Contribution Deliver high-quality program management and strategic consulting support across Nota Consulting client engagements.
Build strong client relationships and identify opportunities where Nota Consulting can provide additional value.
Contribute to business development, proposals, thought leadership, recruiting, and other firm-building activities.
Mentor junior consultants and contribute to the continued development of Nota Consulting's M&A methodologies, tools, and delivery standards.

Required Qualifications 7+ years of professional experience in consulting, program management, M&A, or related transformation roles.
Minimum of 4 years of professional consulting experience working for a consulting firm is required.
Direct experience supporting M&A programs is required, including integrations, carve-outs, divestitures, TSA programs, or transaction-related value creation.
Demonstrated experience managing complex, cross-functional programs with multiple simultaneous workstreams and senior executive stakeholders.
Strong experience developing and managing integrated project plans using Smartsheet, Microsoft Project, Jira, or comparable program management tools.
Ability to independently structure ambiguous problems, develop an execution approach, and drive teams toward decisions and results.
Strong executive presence with exceptional written communication, presentation, facilitation, and stakeholder-management skills.
Ability to perform effectively in high-pressure environments with demanding transaction timelines and periods of elevated workload.
Demonstrated ownership mentality, attention to detail, responsiveness, and commitment to delivering against critical deadlines.
Bachelor's degree required.
Must be based in or able to commute to the Washington, DC area and work from the office four days per week.

Preferred Qualifications Experience with multiple types of M&A programs, including both integration and carve-out/separation engagements.
Experience with Transition Service Agreements (TSAs), Day 1 readiness, IMO/SMO leadership, synergy realization, or value creation programs.
Experience working with private equity firms and/or private equity portfolio companies.
Experience in manufacturing, industrial, technology, SaaS, data and analytics, or business services environments.
PMP certification preferred.
Prosci or other Organizational Change Management certification is a plus.

Compensation & Benefits Nota Consulting offers a comprehensive benefits package including:
Competitive Salary
Medical Insurance, including fully paid employee premiums
Dental Insurance
Vision Insurance
Company-paid Life Insurance
401(k) Match up to 4% of salary
Annual reimbursement of up to $1,000 for professional licenses, certifications, and continuing education

Eligibility to participate in Nota Consulting's performance and business development bonus program

jobs.title: Grantmaking Program Manager
jobs.description:
About The Job

Grantmaking Program Manager

Title: Grantmaking Program Manager

Job code: 8223GG

Employee Group: Civil Service (exempt) Full/Part Time (FTE): Full Time (100% FTE)

Regular/Temporary: Regular

About The Job

The University of Minnesota’s Institute on the Environment (IonE) is seeking a Grantmaking Program Manager to lead the planning, implementation, and continuous improvement of the Institute’s grantmaking portfolio. This position manages the full lifecycle of IonE’s competitive funding programs – including Impact Goals Grants , Mini Grants , and other strategic funding opportunities – from program design and Requests for Proposals (RFPs) through application review, award administration, stewardship, reporting, evaluation, and closeout.

Working collaboratively across IonE’s leadership, research, communications, finance, and administrative teams, the Grantmaking Program Manager serves as the central operational lead for IonE’s grantmaking portfolio – coordinating complex funding cycles, supporting applicants, reviewers, coaches, and funded project teams, and maintaining the authoritative record of the funded portfolio. This position also advances IonE’s strategic commitment to outcomes and impact by developing the metrics, analysis, and reporting that demonstrate portfolio results and inform future funding decisions. Professionals with experience as Program Officers, Program Representatives, Grants Managers, or similar grantmaking roles in foundation, nonprofit, or government funding organizations will find many familiar elements in this position.

The Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is an organized project manager, analytical thinker, and relationship builder who enjoys running complex processes exceptionally well while continually looking for ways to improve them. They are naturally curious about the people, ideas, and projects that make up the portfolio and are energized by identifying opportunities to strengthen programs, enhance participant experiences, and increase organizational impact.

They balance strategic thinking with operational excellence - keeping one eye on the long-term evolution of IonE’s grantmaking portfolio while ensuring the day-to-day work is executed with consistency, accuracy, and efficiency. Comfortable navigating both ambiguity and detail, they embrace continuous learning, seek out opportunities for innovation, and build scalable systems that support the portfolio as it evolves. As IonE’s grantmaking portfolio expands in scope and complexity through future funding opportunities and institutional priorities, this position offers meaningful opportunities for the successful candidate to assume broader strategic leadership and organizational impact.

Informational Job Webinar

Register to attend an informational webinar hosted by the supervisor for this position, Director of Administration & Operations April Deinken . We'll share more about the role, what it's like to work at IonE, and answer questions submitted by prospective applicants through the Zoom registration form.

Attendance is completely optional and does not factor into consideration of your application. The webinar is simply an opportunity to learn more about the position and IonE, and to help you determine whether the role feels like a good mutual fit.

When: Wednesday, Sept. 9, 4:00 - 4:45 p.m. CST
Where: Zoom, webinar format
Link to Register

Salary

The salary range for this position is $74k - $86k/yr ($35.65/hr - $41.53/hr). IonE uses a structured compensation approach that considers a position’s salary range as well as a candidate’s relevant experience, skills, and demonstrated proficiency when determining starting salary.

This hiring range reflects an entry-to-intermediate proficiency level for the position. Candidates entering the role may still be developing some position-specific knowledge and skills, while candidates placed toward the higher end of the hiring range would be expected to demonstrate greater proficiency and independence in the core competencies of the position. Employees may progress through the position’s broader salary range over time as they develop greater proficiency and independence, with salary increases considered through the University’s annual merit process and compensation processes.

Work Schedule & Authorization

Work hours are standard office hours, M–F. IonE and the Research and Innovation Office endorse a work with flexibility approach that offers a welcoming and flexible work environment where everyone is inspired to do their best.

This position has been designated as eligible for flexible work profile 2: Profile 2 is expected to work in the office at least 3 days per week (Mon, Wed, Thu), and typically working remotely 1-2 days per week (Tue, Fri). Your office location will be located at 1954 Buford Ave, Saint Paul, MN 55108. IonE management retains the right to modify flexible work arrangement agreements on a temporary or permanent basis for any reason at any time.

The candidate must reside locally; IonE can potentially provide up to $1,500 of relocation assistance for the ideal candidate. If you currently reside out-of-state and are willing to relocate to the Mpls-St.Paul area, please indicate as much in your cover letter.

Applicants must currently be authorized to work in the United States. IonE is unable to provide employment-based visa sponsorship for this position.

Responsibilities

Grantmaking Program Management (50%)

Run the funding cycles: Lead IonE’s competitive funding programs from program design through award notification, maintaining the systems that keep those cycles consistent and repeatable.

Develop and manage the annual grantmaking calendar, establishing timelines, priorities, and dependencies across IonE’s funding portfolio
Develop and refine RFPs, application materials, review criteria, award documentation, Terms & Conditions, and reporting requirements
Coordinate application and review processes, including recruiting and orienting reviewers, matching reviewers to proposals based on expertise and conflicts of interest, developing award recommendations, and award notifications
Develop resources, guidance, tools, and training materials that enable applicants, reviewers, and coaches to participate successfully throughout the funding lifecycle
Develop and maintain the workflows, templates, standard operating procedures, and records that promote consistency and continuity across grantmaking programs
Collaborate with leadership, research, communications, finance, and administrative staff to align funding cycles with IonE priorities and operational capacity
Continuously assess grantmaking processes and participant experiences, identifying opportunities to improve funding models, eligibility criteria, policies, and practices that strengthen the effectiveness, accessibility, equity, and overall participant experience of IonE’s grantmaking programs

Award Stewardship & Portfolio Records (30%)

Steward funded projects: Serve as the primary relationship holder for funded teams and keep the record of the portfolio accurate and current.

Serve as the primary point of contact for applicants, reviewers, coaches, and funded project teams throughout the funding lifecycle Coordinate award setup, reporting schedules, amendments, no-cost extensions, rebudget requests, and project closeout
Monitor project progress, budgets, expenditures, and compliance with award requirements, proactively engaging with project teams to support timely reporting and milestone completion
Maintain the authoritative record of funded projects, including updating IonE’s public-facing project directory throughout the lifecycle, in accordance with web content standards
Partner with IonE’s public interest communications team by providing regular updates on project milestones, findings, and other storytelling opportunities, and by flagging project directory changes that affect editorial content
Coordinate the collection of project outputs, photos, testimonials, and other assets that support impact reporting and storytelling
Coordinate grant coaching meetings, workshops, and other stewardship activities that support funded teams

Portfolio Evaluation & Reporting (20%)

Measure and communicate impact: Develop the metrics and analyses that show what the portfolio produces and inform what it funds next.

Develop and refine portfolio-wide metrics, evaluation frameworks, and reporting processing aligned with IonE’s strategic priorities
Analyze qualitative and quantitative portfolio data to identify trends, outcomes, and opportunities for continuous improvement
Produce reports and portfolio analyses that inform leadership decisions and provide evidence of the Institute’s impact to internal and external audiences
Assess portfolio performance and outcomes to identify opportunities for continuous improvement and inform future funding priorities and program design
Identify emerging themes and success stories across the grant portfolio to inform strategic planning and communications

General Responsibilities

Like all IonE staff, the Grantmaking Program Manager participates in IonE-wide initiatives, staff meetings, events, and professional development activities; contributes to a collaborative, inclusive, and service-oriented organizational culture; and performs other duties as assigned.

Strong candidates will demonstrate...

A track record of running deadline-driven processes from start to finish: cycles, cohorts, or campaigns that shipped on time, repeatedly
A commitment to follow-through on the unglamorous middle: chasing late reports, closing loops, keeping records current without being asked
The ability to serve as the primary point of contact for a complex portfolio while remaining responsive, organized, and composed across multiple stakeholders and competing priorities
A strong service orientation toward the people inside of a process; ensuring applicants, reviewers, and grantees experience interactions as helpful, clear, and fair
A habit of documenting work and improving systems as they go, leaving processes stronger and more sustainable over time
Fluency moving between operational detail and strategic perspective, recognizing patterns in portfolio data and communicating insights clearly to diverse audiences
Sound judgment about when to resolve issues independently, when to seek input, and when to escalate concerns
Curiosity and a continuous improvement mindset, with a proactive approach to building relationships and developing a deep understanding of the people, projects, and outcomes across the portfolio to effectively represent the work and identify opportunities to strengthen programs over time.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

BA/BS degree plus at least four years of relevant professional experience, or a combination of related education and work experience totaling eight years
Experience managing multi-phase programs, funding cycles, or similarly complex processes involving hard deadlines and multiple stakeholders
Experience administering grants, awards, contracts, or other funded agreements from either the grantmaking or grant-seeking perspective
Demonstrated ability to build and maintain organized records, workflows, documentation, and operational systems
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience producing clear guidance or reports for varied audiences
Proficiency with common productivity and data tools (e.g., Google Workspace, Excel/Sheets) and the ability to learn new platforms quickly

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in a university, research, philanthropic, or nonprofit funding environment
Experience designing or improving requests for proposals (RFPs), review processes, or reporting requirements
Experience with survey and data-collection tools (e.g., Qualtrics) and analyzing qualitative and quantitative program data
Experience developing metrics, basic data analysis, dashboards, or evaluation

with our customers, prospects, and partners (depending on role). This means you'll have the freedom to create a flexible schedule that caters to your business, team, and personal needs, while being intentional to make the most of time spent together. Those in our remote "home office" roles also have the opportunity to come together in our offices for important moments that matter.

jobs.description:
Building the space between proven and possible, MDA Space is a trusted mission partner to the global space industry. A robotics, satellite systems and geointelligence pioneer with a 55-year+ story of world firsts and more than 450 missions, MDA Space is a global leader in communications satellites, Earth and space observation, and space exploration and infrastructure. The global MDA Space team of more than 3,800 space experts has the knowledge and know-how to turn an audacious customer vision into an achievable mission – bringing to bear a one-of-a-kind mix of experience, engineering excellence and wide-eyed wonder that’s been in our DNA since day one. For those who dream big and push boundaries on the ground and in the stars to change the world for the better, we’ll take you there. For more information, visit www.mda.space.

We’re on the hunt for a Project Manager at our UK office.

MDA Space’s international footprint in the UK creates opportunities to work with some of the most exciting space industrial players in the country. Delivering all three business area capabilities in Geointelligence, Robotics & Space Operations, and Satellite Systems, our UK team provides support to our European-based customers while specializing in the development of advanced space sensors for exploration missions as well as space-based communication technology. As our presence grows overseas, so does our need for new ambitious team players to help us advance our place in the Universe and beyond.

Responsibilities

Ensure suitable standards, processes and controls are followed across all phases of the projects from conceptualization through completion, including planning, and managing technical performance to ensure quality, business, schedule and financial objectives are attained.
Set-out and agree work-packages to ensure all HW/SW needs are delivered with customer satisfaction in mind.
Risk, Assumptions, Issues and Dependencies capture & management
Interfacing with various teams – technical, production, validation, quality; to co-ordinate and de-risk schedules
Contribute to the development of new business opportunities and expansion of existing business opportunities in the space community.
Be comfortable to work across multiple projects for multiple customers.
Be intimately involved in the preparation of proposals, proposal work statements and specifications and operating budgets. Influence contract negotiations and modifications.
Identify project issues through risk and opportunity management and provide leadership and direction in how to develop solutions such as re-allocation of resources or modifying contract specification.
Ensure that feedback from internal and external customers and entities is continually and robust fed back into out processes and approach.
Be comfortable in a fast moving and dynamic environment with whilst being able to remain calm and keep the team focused on the goal.

Required Skills

Suitable candidates will ideally have the following attributes:

Direct experience in design and development of space flight hardware and/or software
Bachelor’s degree in engineering or equivalent
At least 5 years experience managing technical projects.
Excellent written and oral communication
Familiarity with project lifecycle from bid through execution and close down
Familiarity with Project Advantage or other scheduling tools
Ability to motivate people
Self- motivated and able to take initiative
Ability to travel as required
Ability to communicate complex issues clearly to various audiences with technical & non-technical backgrounds
Managing and Reporting on Project Budget and Resources to senior management
Defining, mitigating and managing project risks

Skills Considered An Asset

Familiarity with formal configuration control methods
Experience working on projects in the space industry, including gate/phase reviews
Experience dealing with complex systems, analysis and test
Familiarity with communications payload technologies
Familiarity with international standards, ECSS, etc.
Experience in capture management and proposal writing.

We’re a dream team of purpose-driven, collaborative and passionate people, and we are constantly looking for others to join #TeamMDA to ignite new and innovative approaches to problem-solving that push us forward to improve life on and above Earth. If you’re excited to expand our place in space and driven to inspire the next generation, we’ll take you there.

We have entered a new era of exploration and development, and MDA Space welcomes all who yearn to suit up and be part of it. An equal opportunity employer prizing diversity, integrity and collaboration, we are committed to growing MDA Space’s leadership in this next golden age.

jobs.title: Project Manager II, Early Phase (Canada)
jobs.description:
The Project Manager II, EPTR has the overall responsibility for the successful initiation, planning, execution, monitoring, controlling and closure of assigned clinical trials. The Project Manager II, EPTR oversees and coordinates study resources to ensure compliance with the study budget, project scope and timelines and in accordance with applicable standard operating procedures (SOPs), good clinical practices, regulatory and study-specific requirements. The Project Manager II, EPTR acts as the main line of communication to relevant stakeholders and provides input to feasibility, study design, budget development and ensures progress reporting (resources, budget and timeline).

More specifically, the Project Manager II, Early Phase and Translational Research (EPTR):

Acts as the main point of contact for sponsors, vendors, and internal study teams throughout the lifecycle of a clinical trial.
Works closely with clients at study start-up to understand their goals and help determine the most effective operational approach.
Maintains regular communication with sponsors, study teams, functional departments, clinical sites, and senior management.
Oversees all operational aspects of clinical trials, including timelines, budgets, resources, vendor management, and clinical operations activities, while coordinating deliverables across departments.
Monitors and controls study budgets by tracking hours, reviewing billed time, identifying out-of-scope activities, and supporting change order management.
Provides regular updates to internal and external stakeholders on study progress, including site selection, vendor management, budgets, timelines, quality standards, and risk mitigation efforts.
Leads study start-up activities, including kick-off meetings, Trial Master File (TMF) setup, site selection and activation, vendor onboarding, site contracting, and budget negotiations.
Identifies and manages risks, implements quality control measures, and escalates issues to management, quality assurance, or sponsors when necessary.
Leads client meetings, internal team meetings, and vendor status calls, ensuring meeting minutes are documented, distributed, and filed appropriately.
Oversees the quality of project deliverables, including vendor and subcontractor outputs, and drives continuous improvement in training, execution, and quality processes.
Evaluates differences between planned and actual project outcomes and implements corrective actions when required.
Ensures study-specific training matrices are customized, maintained, and up to date.
Verifies that all team members and service providers receive adequate project training and that training records remain current.
Reviews and approves responses to quality assurance audits to ensure compliance with company procedures and regulatory requirements.
Ensures key study documents and deliverables, such as protocols, informed consent forms, eCRFs, source document templates, tables/listings/figures, and clinical study reports, are completed on schedule and meet study requirements.
Oversees the filing, maintenance, and archiving of study documentation within the TMF in compliance with company SOPs and regulatory requirements.
Provides project status updates while ensuring compliance with budgets, scope, timelines, SOPs, Good Clinical Practice (GCP), regulatory requirements, and study-specific procedures.
Tracks recruitment performance and develops mitigation plans when enrollment timelines are at risk.
Participates in the planning and execution of Investigator Meetings.
Works with Regulatory Affairs to ensure ethics submissions are completed on time and that essential documents are collected and maintained throughout the study.
Ensures the TMF remains complete, accurate, and inspection-ready at all times.
May oversee clinical monitoring activities, including site qualification, initiation, routine monitoring, and close-out visits, as well as CRA training and monitoring oversight.
Supports study sites and ensures they have the necessary materials and resources to conduct the study effectively.
Collaborates with Data Management to ensure CRFs meet protocol and sponsor requirements and that data review and query resolution remain on schedule through database lock.
Partners with Clinical Operations to ensure monitoring activities are completed according to sponsor expectations, SOPs, regulations, GCP, and study requirements.
Contributes to the development of Clinical Monitoring Plans.
Provides project-specific training to Clinical Research Associates (CRAs) and may conduct site initiation visits for single-site studies.
Develops annotated site visit reports and monitoring tools, including source data verification worksheets.
May mentor junior staff and support the onboarding of new employees.
Provides technical, therapeutic, and project management expertise to support departmental training and process improvement initiatives.
May participate in business development activities, including client meetings, proposal defenses, RFIs, and RFP responses.
May contribute to process improvement initiatives, including the development, testing, and implementation of operational tools and processes.

Requirements:

A Bachelor's degree (B.Sc.) in a field related to clinical research. A Master's degree (M.Sc.) or Ph.D. is considered an asset.
At least 5 years of experience in the clinical research industry, including a minimum of 3 years of project management experience in Phase I and Phase II clinical trials.
Experience managing multiple clinical trials simultaneously across several study sites.
Previous experience in dermatology clinical trials, which is strongly preferred.
Strong knowledge of Good Clinical Practice (GCP), International Council for Harmonisation (ICH) guidelines, FDA requirements, and applicable local regulations.
Proficiency with the Microsoft Office Suite.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
Bilingualism in English and French is highly desirable.
The ability to work effectively in a collaborative team environment and build strong relationships with colleagues, sponsors, and other stakeholders.
Strong problem-solving, critical-thinking, and creative-thinking skills.
Solid scientific understanding and clinical research knowledge.
Broad cross-functional knowledge of clinical research operations.
The ability to manage multiple projects, prioritize competing demands, and perform effectively under pressure while meeting deadlines.
Knowledge of Good Clinical Practices as well as applicable Health Canada and FDA regulations and guidelines.

Our company:

The Work Environment

At Indero, you will work with brilliant and driven colleagues. Our values are collaboration, innovation, reliability, and responsiveness. We offer a stimulating work environment and attractive opportunities for advancement.

In this position, you will be eligible for the following perks:

Flexible work schedule
Permanent full-time position
Comprehensive benefits (medical, dental, vision, RRSP, vacation, personal days, virtual medical clinic, public transportation rebates, social activities)
Ongoing learning and development opportunities

﻿Work Location

The successful candidate for this position has the option to work remotely anywhere in Canada, or from our headquarters in Montreal (in accordance with company policies and public health directives).

Occasional visits to our Montreal office may be required or encouraged.

About Indero

Indero is a CRO specialized in clinical trials. Based in Montreal, we have built a strong reputation for the quality of our research and services that exceed client expectations. Indero continues to grow and expand across North America and Europe.

Indero is committed to providing equitable treatment and equal opportunity to all individuals. Accommodations are available throughout the recruitment and selection process for applicants with disabilities, upon request.

Please note that Indero only accepts applicants who are legally authorized to work in Canada.
