Modern Technology Solutions, Inc. (MTSI) is searching for a Cybersecurity Systems Analyst - Senior
in support of United States Space Force (USSF) Space Systems Command (SSC) and Combat Forces Command (CFC) Defensive Cyber Operations.

A Cybersecurity Systems Analyst in this context is responsible for continuously assessing, monitoring, and reporting on the operational health, readiness, and effectiveness of Defensive Cyber Operations for Space (DCO-S) capabilities. This includes both internal (enterprise/home-station) systems and external (field/operational site) deployments.

The Cybersecurity Systems Analyst focuses on analyzing, assessing, and strengthening the security posture of information systems through continuous evaluation of cybersecurity controls, vulnerabilities, and risks. The Cybersecurity Systems Analyst supports the full system lifecycle by performing security assessments, implementing and validating technical controls, and ensuring compliance with federal cybersecurity standards (including NIST SP 800-53 and the Risk Management Framework). Has an in-depth understanding of cybersecurity policies, procedures, and technical architectures for government-sector information systems, with sufficient hands-on knowledge to implement and sustain them. Provides technical security guidance and analysis in collaboration with system owners, ISSOs, engineers, and stakeholders, while supporting secure system development, cloud environments, and operational needs. This position may require privileged access and DoD 8570/8140 restrictions will apply.

Role And Responsibilities

Internal DCO-S Capability Health Assessment
Continuously monitor the operational status, performance, and availability of enterprise DCO-S tools, sensors, platforms, and infrastructure.
Conduct regular health checks, configuration audits, and performance analysis on DCO-S systems to identify degradation, misconfigurations, or emerging issues.
Analyze system logs, metrics, and alerts to evaluate the overall cybersecurity posture and effectiveness of internal DCO-S capabilities.
Track and report on key health indicators (availability, latency, detection coverage, false-positive rates, patch compliance, etc.).
Support vulnerability scanning, STIG compliance validation, and remediation tracking for DCO-S systems hosted in enterprise environments.
Maintain accurate documentation of system baselines, configurations, and health trends for internal DCO-S assets.
External / Field / Operational Site DCO-S Health Assessment
Assess the operational health and readiness of DCO-S capabilities deployed at remote or operational sites (including deployable kits, forward-based systems, and site-specific installations).
Coordinate with field operators and site personnel to collect health status data, performance metrics, and issue reports from operational locations.
Perform or support remote and on-site evaluations of deployed DCO-S tools to verify functionality, connectivity, sensor coverage, and alignment with mission requirements.
Identify capability gaps, degraded performance, or sustainment issues affecting DCO-S systems in the field.
Support troubleshooting, configuration validation, and restoration of DCO-S capabilities at operational sites when issues are detected.
Track the status of deployable DCO-S systems (e.g., readiness of kits, software versions, hardware health) across multiple locations.
Analysis, Reporting & Continuous Improvement
Develop and maintain dashboards, status reports, and briefings on the overall health of DCO-S capabilities (internal + external).
Analyze trends and root causes of capability degradation; recommend corrective actions, process improvements, or technical mitigations.
Support risk assessments related to DCO-S system health that could impact mission readiness or defensive cyber operations.
Collaborate with system owners, ISSOs, engineers, and operational units to ensure DCO-S capabilities remain effective and mission-ready.
Assist in the validation of security controls and continuous monitoring activities specifically tied to DCO-S platforms.
Contribute to after-action reviews and lessons-learned processes following exercises, deployments, or real-world events involving DCO-S systems.
Coordination & Support
Serve as a technical point of contact for DCO-S health and readiness questions from leadership, operators, and supporting organizations.
Coordinate with external stakeholders (site teams, higher headquarters, vendors) to resolve health-related issues affecting operational DCO-S capabilities.
Support planning and execution of system upgrades, patches, and configuration changes while minimizing impact on operational availability.

Required

At least 12+ years' related professional experience
Experience analyzing system architectures, identifying security gaps, and recommending technical mitigations.
Familiarity with SIEM tools, log analysis, and basic threat detection/response activities.
Strong written and verbal communication skills for technical documentation, risk reporting, and stakeholder interaction.
Experience deploying, managing, or troubleshooting Docker containers
Familiarity with automation and configuration-management tools such as Ansible
Proficiency in scripting languages such as Python and Bash
Ability to work independently on assigned systems while collaborating effectively in cross-functional teams.
Knowledge of Defense-in-Depth architectures, network security principles, operating system hardening, and cloud security concepts.
Prior experience supporting federal, DoD, or intelligence community systems.
Strong understanding of cybersecurity frameworks and models, including MITRE ATT&CK and the Cyber Kill Chain

Desired

Experience supporting DoD cloud environments at Secret, Top Secret, or SAP levels.
Experience integrating with enterprise DevSecOps platforms such as Platform One, Space CAMP, or other DoD enterprise PaaS environments.
Experience with GitLab, including source control and CI/CD workflows
Experience applying machine learning to cybersecurity or data-analysis use cases

Who We Are

At Corebridge Financial, we believe action is everything. That’s why every day we partner with financial professionals and institutions to make it possible for more people to take action in their financial lives, for today and tomorrow.

We Align To a Set Of Values That Are The Core Pillars That Define Our Culture And Help Bring Our Brand Purpose To Life

We are stronger as one: We collaborate across the enterprise, scale what works and act decisively for our customers and partners.
We deliver on commitments: We are accountable, empower each other and go above and beyond for our stakeholders.
We learn, improve and innovate: We get better each day by challenging the status quo and equipping ourselves for the future.
We are inclusive: We embrace different perspectives, enabling our colleagues to make an impact and bring their whole selves to work.

Who You’ll Work With

The Information Technology organization is the technological foundation of our business and works in collaboration with our partners from across the company. The team drives technology and digital transformation, partners with business leaders to design and execute new strategies through IT and operations services and ensures the necessary IT risk management and security measures are in place and aligned with enterprise architecture standards and principles.

About The Role

As a Senior Investigations Analyst
, you are the lead "digital detective" for the organization. You will be responsible for conducting complex, forensically sound investigations into security breaches, policy violations, and potential litigation matters. You will leverage advanced forensic suites—with a particular focus on Nuix—to parse massive datasets, recover "hidden" evidence, and build a factual narrative for legal, HR, and executive stakeholders.

Responsibilities

Forensic Acquisition & Preservation

Chain of Custody: Lead the collection and preservation of digital evidence (workstations, mobile, cloud, and server logs) ensuring strict adherence to forensic standards and chain-of-custody protocols.
Imaging & Extraction: Perform live and dead-box imaging of systems across diverse OS environments (Windows, macOS, Linux).
Remote Collections: Utilize enterprise forensic tools to perform stealthy, remote data acquisitions without disrupting business operations.

Deep-Dive Investigation & Analysis

Axiom/Nuix Power User: Utilize forensic toolsets to ingest, process, and analyze multi-terabyte datasets. You will be expected to create complex search queries, perform deduplication, and identify communication patterns across disparate data sources.
Artifact Analysis: Investigate system artifacts (e.g. Registry, MFT, Shellbags, LNK files) to reconstruct user activity and timeline events.
Data Recovery: Perform file carving and unallocated space analysis to recover deleted or obscured evidence.
Email & Communication Forensics: Conduct deep-dive analysis of PST/OST files and cloud-based mail (O365/Gmail) to identify evidence of data exfiltration or collusion.

Reporting & Stakeholder Management

Expert Reporting: Translate technical forensic findings into clear, "plain English" investigative reports suitable for legal proceedings or executive review.
Interdisciplinary Collaboration: Act as the technical liaison for Legal, HR, and Internal Audit teams to define the scope of investigations and provide status updates on high-sensitivity cases.
Continuous Improvement: Refine forensic workflows and laboratory standards to ensure the team stays ahead of anti-forensic techniques.

Skills And Qualifications

Technical Requirements

Experience: 4+ years of experience in digital forensics and/or corporate investigations.
Forensic Toolset Mastery:
Axiom or Nuix (Highly Preferred)
Other Tools: Advanced experience with at least two of the following: EnCase, FTK, Autopsy or X-Ways Forensics.
Mobile Forensics: Experience with Cellebrite UFED or Magnet GrayKey.
DLP: Purview

Technical Knowledge

Deep understanding of file systems (NTFS, APFS, Ext4), memory forensics (Volatility), and cloud-native logging (Azure Unified Audit Log, AWS CloudTrail).
Scripting (Plus): Basic ability to use Python or SQL to automate data parsing or query large investigative databases.
Preferred Certifications
Tool-Specific: Nuix Workstation Forensic Practitioner, EnCE, or MCFE.
Vendor-Neutral: GIAC Certified Forensic Analyst (GCFA), GIAC Network Forensic Analyst (GNFA), or Certified Fraud Examiner (CFE).

Soft Skills

Ethics & Integrity: Unwavering commitment to maintaining confidentiality and impartiality during sensitive investigations.
The "Detective Mindset": The ability to look past the obvious and connect non-linear data points to find the "smoking gun."
Clarity under Pressure: Experience delivering tough findings to senior leadership in high-stress environments.

Central Maine Healthcare (CMH), a member of Prime Healthcare Foundation, is an integrated healthcare delivery system serving approximately 400,000 residents across central, western, and midcoast Maine through a network of more than 40 primary and specialty care locations. Bolt is shaping a future where cities are built for people, not cars. What started as an ambitious project of a 19-year-old in 2013 has grown into a global mobility platform used by more than 200 million customers and 4.5 million driver and courier partners across 50 countries.

From ride-hailing and food delivery to scooters, e-bikes, and car-sharing, Bolt helps people move through cities every day. Small, autonomous teams drive this work, combining the speed and ownership of a startup with the scale of a global technology company backed by more than €1bn in funding.

And we're just getting started.

Why join Bolt?

Build the future of mobility and help transform how people live and move in cities.
Tackle challenges at scale that span technology, operations, regulation, and growth.
Take real ownership early. Small, lean teams mean your decisions matter from day one, and you'll learn fast alongside some of the best people in the industry.

We're hiring a Senior Operations Specialist to drive performance across Bolt's rides marketplace in Poland. This isn't a typical Data Analyst role. Beyond strong analytical skills, we need someone excited to own operational projects end to end: analyzing our product, building deep dives for Bolt's leadership, and getting into the weeds of our financial processes to fix and improve them. It's a chance to build both analytical and business skills, positioning you to become a top business operator in the industry.

You'll dig deep into data, build the case for action, and own execution end to end. You don't just hand off insights, you fix the problem.

In this role you will lead high-stakes analytical and finance projects across supply, demand, pricing, and conversion, identify what's broken and why, and lead the operational interventions that move the numbers. Analysis is the starting point - impact is the goal. You'll partner closely with Finance, Growth, Marketing, and Product, manage relationships with our key Fleet Partners, and design the scalable processes that let the team keep compounding those gains.

Main Tasks And Responsibilities

Own end-to-end marketplace analysis: deep-dive data, build models, and develop dashboards across supply, demand, pricing, and marketplace health.
Diagnose performance issues and translate findings into clear actions, quantifying impact on rides, revenue, and cost.
Understand our financial processes, own them, and drive improvement.
Own execution - design and deliver operational interventions across pricing, incentives, driver engagement, and supply–demand balance.
Act as Account Manager for key Fleet Partners, helping them resolve issues, scale on Bolt, and align on shared performance goals.
Design, document, and improve scalable processes that the wider team can run with, and hold yourself accountable for measurable outcomes.

3–5 years in operations, strategy, or analytical roles (marketplace, mobility, or tech preferred).
Exceptional data analysis and modelling skills - you independently build and interrogate datasets, structure complex problems, and translate findings into action.
Advanced Excel / Google Sheets modelling (forecasting, scenarios, unit economics) and hands-on experience with BI tools (Looker, Power BI, or similar). SQL is a strong plus.
Process-minded and self-sufficient - you design new ways of working rather than just operate within existing ones, and thrive in fast-paced environments with minimal supervision.
Clear, concise communicator in English and Polish, able to influence senior stakeholders and manage external partners with confidence.

Experience is great, but what we really look for is drive, intelligence, and integrity. So even if you don’t tick every box, please consider applying!

Purpose Unlimited
is an independent financial services company with an unrelenting focus on customer-centric innovation, delivered through technology-driven solutions. Led by entrepreneur Som Seif, the company is developing a diversified product platform aimed at addressing historically underserved segments of the market. Purpose Unlimited’s businesses include Purpose Investments, Advisor Solutions by Purpose, and Driven.

Who is Purpose Investments?

Purpose Investments
is an innovation- driven asset management company with over $20 billion under management, offering both managed and quantitative investment products. Much of what is available to the average Canadian investor today is outdated and expensive. Purpose Investments’ goal is to constantly innovate, and make investing simple, intuitive and affordable for everyone.

Vacancy Status:
This is for a current opening.

Compensation:
$90,000 - $105,000

Job Description

The role

The Trading Operations Analyst is the production layer of the trade operations function — responsible for the accurate and timely completion of all post-trade activity across every asset class the desk trades. This includes equities, ETFs, fixed income, derivatives, FX, digital assets, and physical commodities.

This role is for someone who takes precision seriously, escalates early, and approaches their work with a process- improvement mindset. The desk is actively deploying AI tools to automate routine tasks — this person is expected to engage with those tools, validate their outputs, and help identify where they can do more. You do not need to build the tools; you need to use them well.

Securities setup is a meaningful and distinctive part of this role. Private placements, structured instruments, and alternative asset classes need to be correctly established in the book of record before they can trade — this person owns that process.

The Team

The Capital Markets & Trading team operates as a single unit across two functions: trading and trade operations. Both sides of the desk understand the full trade lifecycle — from execution through settlement — and cover each other when it counts. Success in this role requires equal parts transformational leadership, operational excellence, and change management. The ideal candidate will build scalable improvement systems, champion AI-driven innovation, and advance Vendor Operations toward a Frontier Firm model that delivers greater quality, productivity, customer satisfaction, and business value.

This is not a traditional Continuous Improvement role focused solely on Lean methodologies. It is a transformation leadership role responsible for helping redefine how operations are designed, executed, measured, and continuously optimized in an AI-first world.

Responsibilities

Capability Portfolio Ownership & Feature Management

Own the strategy, roadmap, prioritization, business cases, implementation governance, adoption, benefits realization, and continuous improvement of a portfolio of artificial intelligence-driven operational capabilities.

AI Transformation & Frontier Firm Enablement

Lead the adoption of AI-first and agentic operating models across Vendor Operations.
Identify opportunities to automate manual processes and improve decision-making through AI-enabled workflows.
Partner with engineering, service design, and operations teams to scale AI and automation capabilities.
Drive operational readiness for Microsoft's Frontier Firm vision.

Continuous Improvement System Deployment

Establish and scale continuous improvement practices across Vendor Operations using Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA), Lean, or other structured problem-solving methodologies.
Build repeatable improvement frameworks that create sustainable operational gains.
Facilitate cross-functional improvement initiatives that drive measurable business impact.
Ensure improvements are standardized and institutionalized through governance and operational rhythms.

Operational Excellence & Performance Management

Define and track metrics that reflect customer value, operational efficiency, quality, productivity, and adoption of AI-enabled capabilities.
Develop performance insights that enable leaders to prioritize investments and improvement opportunities.
Create visibility into operational health and transformation progress through data-driven reporting.

Change Management & Organizational Adoption

Lead adoption strategies for new capabilities, operating models, tools, and ways of working, using stakeholder feedback and performance data to guide ongoing capability improvements.
Partner with stakeholders to remove barriers and accelerate behavioral change.
Ensure improvements transition from pilots to sustainable business practices.
Build organizational capability for continuous learning and improvement.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Influence

Serve as a trusted advisor to Vendor Operations leaders on transformation priorities and continuous improvement strategy.
Align stakeholders across Vendor Operations, Engineering, Service Design, and broader MBO initiatives.
Foster knowledge sharing and reuse of best practices across the vendor ecosystem.
Drive organizational alignment around operational excellence and business outcomes.

Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree in Business, Operations, Finance, or related field AND 4+ years experience in program management, process management, or process improvement OR equivalent experience.

Preferred Qualifications

6+ years of experience leading operational transformation, continuous improvement, or business process optimization initiatives in complex global organizations.
Demonstrated success driving measurable improvements in quality, productivity, customer experience, or operational efficiency.
Strong data-driven decision-making skills with experience defining and managing operational performance metrics.
Proven ability to influence organizational boundaries and lead without direct authority. Strong executive communication, stakeholder management, and leadership skills.
Experience owning a portfolio of operational capabilities or features, including strategy, roadmap planning, prioritization, business case development, implementation governance, adoption, and benefits realization.
Experience deploying AI, automation, or agentic solutions within operational environments.
Experience implementing structured improvement methodologies such as Lean, PDCA, Kaizen, or related frameworks.
Knowledge of vendor operations, outsourcing models, or large-scale service delivery organizations.
Experience partnering with engineering, product, or service design teams on transformation initiatives.

Certification or experience in Lean Six Sigma or comparable continuous improvement disciplines.

new_jobs.description:
Description

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of technical program managers, design engineers, construction managers, network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

The ML Capacity Delivery Team (MLZ) is seeking a Principal Technical Infrastructure Program Manager to define and drive the technical vision, strategy, and roadmap for the systems and tools that enable ML capacity delivery at global scale. In this role, you will serve as the single-threaded technical leader responsible for building, evolving, and scaling the platforms and automation that underpin how we plan, track, and deliver ML infrastructure; from demand signal through rack-level installation.

You will work at the intersection of infrastructure delivery, data engineering, and tooling while partnering with systems engineers, software development teams, Business Intelligence Engineers (BIE), operations leaders, and cross-functional stakeholders to translate complex operational requirements into scalable, reliable systems. The ideal candidate is a seasoned technical leader who thrives in ambiguity, can articulate a compelling 1–3 year technical roadmap, and has a track record of driving cross-organizational alignment to deliver platforms that fundamentally improve how teams operate at scale.

Key job responsibilities

Own the technical vision and multi-year roadmap (1–3 years) for ML Capacity Delivery systems and tools, aligning investments to business priorities and capacity delivery goals across core and Gen AI platforms.
Drive cross-functional alignment across systems engineering, software development, BIE, operations, and planning teams to define requirements, prioritize capabilities, and deliver integrated tooling solutions.
Architect and deliver scalable platforms that automate and optimize capacity delivery workflows; including demand planning, build tracking, supply chain visibility, and operational reporting.
Serve as the technical authority for systems and tools within MLZ, influencing Director/VP-level leadership on investment decisions, build-vs-buy trade-offs, and platform strategy through data-driven business cases.
Identify and eliminate operational friction by mapping end-to-end workflows, quantifying inefficiencies, and delivering automation that reduces manual effort and accelerates delivery velocity.
Establish engineering excellence; define standards for system reliability, data quality, observability, and documentation that enable teams to build and operate with confidence at scale.
Force-multiply across the organization by creating reusable frameworks, mechanisms, and best practices that elevate the effectiveness of multiple teams and programs simultaneously.
Drive clarity in highly ambiguous environments where the business strategy, architectural approach, and problem definition may not yet exist. While decomposing complex challenges into actionable execution plans.
Build and maintain strategic partnerships with internal platform teams, data engineering organizations, and tooling providers to ensure MLZ systems integrate seamlessly with the broader AWS infrastructure ecosystem.
Establish metrics, dashboards, and reporting mechanisms to provide stakeholders and senior leadership clear insight into platform health, delivery timelines, adoption, and business impact.

About The Team

*Why AWS*

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

*Diverse Experiences*

Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

*Work/Life Balance*

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

*Inclusive Team Culture*

Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

*Mentorship and Career Growth*

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Basic Qualifications

10+ years of program management, tech program management, or related experience
10+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
Experience defining roadmap strategy and prioritizing deliverables for your team products
4+ years of designing or architecting (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
Bachelor's degree or above in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Information Management, Information Systems, or other related discipline

Experience managing programs across cross-functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working in data centers or critical infrastructure
Experience in automation or monitoring frameworks, deployment or development
Experience performing complex business case analysis to justify technical decisions and presenting the justification to management in a high-level review
Experience communicating and presenting to senior leadership

Experience with AI/ML infrastructure, GPU/accelerator deployments, or high-performance computing environments

Track record of driving technical standardization and process improvement across globally distributed teams

MBA or Master's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or related field

Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner.

The base salary range for this position is listed below. Your Amazon package will include sign-on payments and restricted stock units (RSUs). Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location. Amazon also offers comprehensive benefits including health insurance (medical, dental, vision, prescription, Basic Life & AD&D insurance and option for Supplemental life plans, EAP, Mental Health Support, Medical Advice Line, Flexible Spending Accounts, Adoption and Surrogacy Reimbursement coverage), 401(k) matching, paid time off, and parental leave. Learn more about our benefits at https://amazon.jobs/en/benefits.

new_jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Silicon
new_jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

Anthropic is building custom silicon for Claude. The hardware our models run on is one of the most direct levers we have on capability, cost, and reliability — and we've decided to take design authority over it ourselves.

We're looking for a Technical Program Manager to own end-to-end execution of our silicon, from architecture definition through tapeout, first-silicon bring-up, and production ramp. You'll be working alongside a small group of domain experts across front-end design, verification, physical design, DFT, analog/mixed-signal, foundry, and packaging. There is no process to inherit — you'll build the execution machinery this program runs on.

This is a partner-heavy program by design. You'll drive a portfolio of external engagements — ASIC design services, IP vendors, foundry, and OSAT. You should have shipped chips before, know what a realistic silicon schedule looks like and its failure modes, and be comfortable making consequential program calls without a large organization behind you. And because this is Anthropic, you'll have Claude as a collaborator — we expect the TPMs on this team to push hard on what AI-assisted program management can look like.

Key responsibilities

Own the integrated silicon program plan — architecture closure, RTL freeze, DV milestones, IP delivery, PD closure, DFT, tapeout, and post-silicon bring-up.
Drive external partner execution across ASIC design partners, IP vendors, foundry, and packaging/test.
Run technology and IP selection as a program: track candidate vendors and options, drive evaluations to a decision, and land the build / buy / license calls with engineering leadership.
Build the execution mechanisms a silicon team needs — milestone definitions, risk and dependency tracking, design reviews, release management, exec reporting — and keep them lightweight enough that engineers actually use them.
Manage the interface between silicon and its consumers: hardware systems for package/board/bring-up, and inference/kernels/compiler teams for hardware-software co-design, so trade-offs land as coordinated decisions rather than late surprises.
Own the post-silicon program — bring-up planning, ATE/test handoff, sample distribution, validation, and the path to production readiness.
Develop and share AI-assisted approaches to program management — schedule and dependency modeling, spec and milestone consistency checking, partner-deliverable tracking, status synthesis.

Minimum Qualifications

8+ years in silicon/SoC program management, chip lead, or an equivalent role that owned a chip schedule end to end.
Direct ownership of at least one program that taped out and reached production, with milestones you can speak to in detail — including where it slipped and what you did about it.
Working technical fluency across the silicon lifecycle — front-end, DV, PD, DFT, foundry, packaging.
Experience running external silicon partners — ASIC houses, IP vendors, foundry, or OSAT — including SOW scoping, delivery tracking, and escalation.
Track record of building program mechanisms from scratch on an ambiguous, fast-moving effort.
Strong written communication — plans, reviews, and exec updates that many teams depend on.
Comfort operating with high autonomy and limited process on a highly dynamic program.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience on ML accelerators, high-performance compute, networking, or other large, high-bandwidth SoCs at advanced process nodes.
Experience on a first-generation or early silicon program, including standing up flows, methodology, or vendor relationships from nothing.
Experience with both partner-executed and fully in-house programs, and a view on the trade-offs between them.
Prior hands-on engineering background in one or more silicon domains (design, DV, PD, DFT, or SI/PI).
Familiarity with the chip-package-system interface and co-design with a hardware systems team.
Experience with hardware-software co-design programs — working directly with compiler, kernel, or runtime teams.
Practical experience using AI tools in your own workflow, and clear ideas about where they help and where they don't.
BS/MS in EE, CE, CS, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary

$365,000—$435,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues.
